test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 11 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which author's "Small Things Like These" was shortlisted for the 2022 Booker Prize but is NOT of Indian origin?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Claire Keegan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Claire Keegan** is a distinguished **Irish author** whose work **Small Things Like These** achieved significant recognition by being **shortlisted** for the **2022 Booker Prize**.
 
• The novella is notably the **shortest book** in the history of the **Booker Prize** to ever be shortlisted, containing approximately **116 pages**.
 
• The narrative is set in **1985** in **New Ross, Ireland**, and follows the life of **Bill Furlong**, a coal merchant who uncovers the disturbing secrets of a local **Magdalene Laundry** run by the church.
 
• While the **2022 Booker Prize** featured authors from diverse backgrounds, **Claire Keegan** represents **Ireland** and does not have **Indian origin**, unlike other prominent Booker winners often associated with the region.
 
• The book won the **Orwell Prize for Political Fiction** in **2022** and explores themes of **complicity**, **courage**, and **social injustice** within a small-town religious community.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arundhati Roy**:

 
 
• An **Indian author** and activist who achieved global fame by winning the **Booker Prize** in **1997**.
 
• Her award-winning novel, **The God of Small Things**, is a seminal work in **Indian English literature**.
 
 
 
• **Shehan Karunatilaka**:
 
 
• A **Sri Lankan** writer who was the actual **winner** of the **2022 Booker Prize**.
 
• He won the award for his supernatural satire titled **The Seven Moons of Maali Almeida**.
 
 
 
• **Elizabeth Strout**:
 
 
• A celebrated **American novelist** who was also on the **2022 Booker Prize** shortlist.
 
• She was nominated for her novel **Oh William!** and is previously a **Pulitzer Prize** winner for **Olive Kitteridge**.
 
 
 
• **Magdalene Laundries**:
 
 
• Historical institutions in **Ireland** that operated from the **18th to the late 20th century**, which serve as the grim historical backdrop for Keegan's novella.
